content: Visit note | 2025-01-06 12:00 PM | Dr. Fahmida Yasmin, ENT | Patient: Nayeem Hossain, 34, male. Mr. Hossain, a bus driver, attends with a sore throat that has lasted three days, and swallowing has become painful enough that he avoids solid food. He also reports fever with chills, especially at night. The symptoms began soon after he drank cold beverages at a wedding in Savar. He has no long-term illnesses. He denies earache, cough, and difficulty breathing. On examination: temperature 102.5°F, BP 131/81 mmHg, pulse 109 bpm, weight 64 kg. Both tonsils are enlarged, red, and covered with a few white spots, and the throat is generally inflamed. The neck is supple with no swelling. Assessment: Acute tonsillitis. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to gargle with warm salt water, eat soft food, and drink plenty of fluids. Follow-up in 1 week.
